subject: Re: SpectralTech capacity needs — ephemeral GPU slab & surge commitments
messages:
From: Kerry Liu <kerry.liu@spectraltech.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Rao <asha.rao@spectraltech.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity question — product launch surge

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed by the latency numbers. We have an upcoming product launch (mid-September) and need a mix of guaranteed dedicated capacity for steady traffic plus the ability to surge for short windows (hours) during marketing-driven spikes.

Two asks to start:
- Can Redwood commit to an "ephemeral slab" model — i.e., a reserved baseline + ability to attach temporary GPU slabs for 4–12 hour windows that scale to a defined multiplier?
- What SLAs or credits would apply if the transient slabs are unavailable at time-of-need? We need a practical plan for launch days.

Also copying procurement (Asha) so we can coordinate contract language.

Best,
Kerry Liu
Head of Platform, SpectralTech

---
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Kerry Liu <kerry.liu@spectraltech.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Asha Rao <asha.rao@spectraltech.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question — product launch surge

Kerry — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can support a reserved baseline plus short-duration slabs that attach to the Dedicated pool and then detach after the surge window. I attached a capacity matrix and a draft term sheet to this thread for the proposed structure.

High-level proposal:
- Baseline: 8 reserved GPUs (pinned to your Dedicated pool) for predictable steady traffic.
- Ephemeral slabs: up to 24 GPUs available in 4-, 8-, or 12-hour increments. These are elastic allocations that can be requested via API or scheduled in advance.
- Surge multiplier: the slab can scale the effective throughput by 3x compared to baseline, subject to model and sequence length. We provide estimated RPS/token throughput in the attached matrix.
- Protection: automatic fallback to a compatible lower-capacity runtime (lower-quant perf profile) if ephemeral slabs are constrained.

SLA/credits note: Our standard Dedicated SLA covers baseline availability. For ephemeral slabs we can offer a target availability commitment for scheduled windows (e.g., 99% availability for scheduled slabs) with a proportional credit if we miss the window or fail to attach within 15 minutes of the start of the scheduled window. Marcus and Rishi — can you confirm the feasibility of 15-minute attach target and the failure-mode behavior?

Next steps: If SpectralTech agrees with the structure, we can lock in slab sizes and cadence, then hand to legal for the draft amendment. Asha — happy to sync offline on the commercial language.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: spectral-capacity-matrix-v3.xlsx (Excel)
Attachment: ephemeral-slab-terms-draft.pdf (PDF)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 13:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question — product launch surge

Kerry/Vanessa — quick technical clarifications from infra:
- Attach latency: for scheduled slabs we can guarantee attach within 10–15 minutes, provided global capacity headroom is available and the slab was reserved in advance. For on-demand (ad hoc API requests) attach latency can vary; typical median is ~4 minutes but can spike depending on cloud provisioning and regional capacity.
- Fallback behavior: if slab attach fails, requests are routed to your baseline or a lower-performance model variant; we keep a per-token degradation log you can ingest for post-mortem.
- Billing & metering: ephemeral slabs bill by the minute once attached; unused pre-scheduled slabs that are not attached due to capacity constraints can be credited at a configurable rate (proposed 50% credit for missed scheduled hours).

Open engineering item: we need to define exact metrics that trigger an automatic fallback (queue depth, attach timeout). Proposal: attach timeout = 15 minutes; queue depth threshold = 120 concurrent requests for the baseline model. If those thresholds are hit and slab not attachable, route to fallback runtime and mark events.

I can add these details to the term ops sheet if you want them in writing.

—Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Vanessa/Kerry — procurement questions so we can move to contracting: 
1) Can the ephemeral slabs be pre-reserved as part of the deal (we'd like guaranteed slots for three launch days across Q3) and if so how are they invoiced?
2) If Redwood fails to provide an attached slab for a pre-reserved window, what is the credit calculation and is there a credit cap?
3) Are there any minimum usage or early-termination charges tied to the baseline + slab structure?

Please include a short example invoice line (baseline charge, ephemeral slab hourly rate, credit example). We need that for budget sign-off.

Thanks,
Asha Rao
VP, Procurement | SpectralTech

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question — product launch surge

Asha/Kerry — summary and concrete items for contracting and ops: 
1) Commercial structure (example invoice lines):
   - Baseline reserved capacity: 8 GPUs, monthly retainer = $28,000 (example)
   - Ephemeral slab (hourly): $120/GPU/hour for attached hours; billed by the minute pro rata.
   - Missed scheduled slab credit: 50% of the slab-hours not provided (cap: credits cannot exceed 20% of monthly spend unless otherwise negotiated).
2) Reservations & billing: you can pre-reserve named slab windows (we'll hold capacity for those windows) and they appear as pre-scheduled line items on monthly invoice. Pre-reserving without attaching is billable at a reduced standby rate (25%) unless credit applied for failure to attach.
3) SLAs & attach guarantees: engineering confirms target attach of 10–15 minutes for scheduled slabs. For contract language we'll propose: scheduled slab availability target = 99% for pre-reserved windows; remedy = slab-hour credit at 50% of slab charge for missed availability.
4) Ops runbook items (action owners):
   - Marcus: add attach-time metrics and fallback event logs to the shared runbook (ETA: 7 days).
   - Rishi: capacity guardbanding policy for your account; propose 1.25x safety headroom for scheduled launches.
   - Vanessa/Lauren: finalize slab sizes and pricing with Asha; prepare amendment and DocuSign link.

If that sounds good, Lauren and I will route a one-page amendment and an example invoice. We'll also add a shared Slack channel for launch-day ops.

Thanks — will follow up with the amendment and the DocuSign link.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
